sentences.zh: 鄒緝，字仲熙，吉水人。

translations.literal: Zou Ji, styled Zhongxi, was a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Ji, whose style was Zhongxi, came from Jishui.

sentences.zh: 洪武中舉明經，授星子教諭。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu reign he passed the examination in the Classics and was appointed instructor at Xingzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era he passed the Classics examination and was made instructor at Xingzi.

sentences.zh: 建文時入為國子助教。

translations.literal: In the Jianwen era he entered service as an assistant instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jianwen emperor he entered the capital as an assistant instructor at the National University.

sentences.zh: 成祖即位，擢翰林侍講。

translations.literal: When the Yongle Emperor took the throne, Ji was promoted to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yongle Emperor came to power, he was promoted to Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 立東宮，兼左中允，屢署國子監事。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was established, he also served as Left Vice-Director of the Household and repeatedly acted as Superintendent of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the heir apparent was installed, he also held the post of Left Vice-Director of the Household and often served in an acting capacity as Superintendent of the National University.

sentences.zh: 永樂十九年，三殿災，詔求直言，緝上疏曰：

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Yongle, the three main halls burned; an edict called for forthright counsel, and Ji submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year of Yongle, fire destroyed the three main halls; the throne called for frank counsel, and Ji submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 陛下肇建北京，焦勞聖慮，幾二十年。

translations.literal: Your Majesty first established Beijing and has borne the imperial cares with anxious toil for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty first raised Beijing as the capital and has borne the cares of state with anxious toil for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 工大費繁，調度甚廣，冗官蠶食，耗費國儲。

translations.literal: The works are vast and the expenses heavy; requisitions are very broad; superfluous officials gnaw away like silkworms, draining the national stores.
translations.idiomatic: The construction is vast and costly, requisitions reach everywhere, redundant officials nibble away at revenue, and the national treasury is drained.

sentences.zh: 工作之夫，動以百萬，終歲供役，不得躬親田畝以事力作。

translations.literal: Laborers on the works number in the millions; they labor in corvée all year and cannot themselves tend their fields to do productive work.
translations.idiomatic: Laborers on the works run into the millions; conscripted for service all year long, they cannot work their own fields with their own hands.

sentences.zh: 猶且征求無藝，至伐桑棗以供薪，剝桑皮以為楮。

translations.literal: Moreover levies are boundless, reaching the point of felling mulberry and jujube for firewood and stripping mulberry bark for paper.
translations.idiomatic: On top of that, levies know no limit—mulberry and jujube are cut for fuel, and mulberry bark is stripped to make paper.

sentences.zh: 加之官吏橫征，日甚一日。

translations.literal: Added to this, officials levy arbitrarily, day by day more severe.
translations.idiomatic: To this are added the arbitrary exactions of officials, which grow worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 如前歲買辦顏料，本非土產，動科千百。

translations.literal: As in the year before last, when pigments were purchased on commission though they were not local products, households were levied by the hundreds and thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Take the purchase of pigments the year before last: they were not local products, yet levies ran into the hundreds and thousands of households.

sentences.zh: 民相率斂鈔，購之他所。

translations.literal: The people together pooled paper money to buy them elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The people pooled their paper notes and bought the pigments elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 大青一斤，價至萬六千貫。

translations.literal: For one jin of great blue, the price reached sixteen thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: A single pound of azurite cost as much as sixteen thousand strings of cash.

sentences.zh: 及進納，又多留難，往復展轉，當須二萬貫鈔，而不足供一柱之用。

translations.literal: When it was delivered, officials again raised difficulties; going back and forth, it might take twenty thousand strings of paper money and still not suffice for one pillar's use.
translations.idiomatic: When it was delivered, officials obstructed and delayed again and again; after all the back-and-forth, twenty thousand strings might still not buy enough for a single pillar.

sentences.zh: 其後既遣官采之產所，而買辦猶未止。

translations.literal: Afterward, although officials were sent to gather it at its place of production, commissioned purchases still did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Later, although officials were sent to collect pigments at the source, commissioned purchases still did not stop.

sentences.zh: 蓋緣工匠多派牟利，而不顧民艱至此。

translations.literal: This was because craftsmen were widely assigned to profit for themselves and paid no heed to the people's hardship, reaching this point.
translations.idiomatic: The reason was that craftsmen were widely assigned to line their own pockets without regard for the people's hardship—hence conditions like these.

sentences.zh: 夫京師天下根本。

translations.literal: The capital is the root of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the root of the empire.

sentences.zh: 人民安則京師安，京師安則國本固而天下安。

translations.literal: When the people are secure, the capital is secure; when the capital is secure, the foundation of the state is firm and the realm is secure.
translations.idiomatic: When the people are at peace, the capital is at peace; when the capital is at peace, the foundation of the state is firm and the realm is secure.

sentences.zh: 自營建以來，工匠小人假托威勢，驅迫移徙，號令方施，廬舍已壞。

translations.literal: Since construction began, petty craftsmen have borrowed authority, driving people to move; the order has scarcely been issued when their dwellings are already destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Since construction began, petty craftsmen have abused their power, forcing people to relocate—the order has barely been issued when their homes are already torn down.

sentences.zh: 孤兒寡婦哭泣叫號，倉皇暴露，莫知所適。

translations.literal: Orphans and widows weep and cry out, exposed in panic, not knowing where to go.
translations.idiomatic: Orphans and widows weep and wail, cast out in panic with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 遷移甫定，又復驅令他徒，至有三四徙不得息者。

translations.literal: Hardly have they settled after relocation when they are driven to move again; some are moved three or four times without rest.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly have they settled when they are driven to move again—some are relocated three or four times without respite.

sentences.zh: 及其既去，而所空之地，經月逾時，工猶未及。

translations.literal: After they have gone, the land they vacated, for months on end, still sees no work begun.
translations.idiomatic: After they have gone, the land they vacated stands idle for months while work has yet to begin.

sentences.zh: 此陛下所不知，而人民疾怨者也。

translations.literal: This is what Your Majesty does not know, and what makes the people bitter and resentful.
translations.idiomatic: This is what Your Majesty does not know—and what fills the people with bitterness and resentment.

sentences.zh: 貪官汙吏，遍布內外，剝削及於骨髓。

translations.literal: Greedy and corrupt officials are spread throughout inside and outside, their exactions reaching to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy, corrupt officials are everywhere, inside and out, stripping the people to the bone.

sentences.zh: 朝廷每遣一人，即是其人養活之計。

translations.literal: Each time the court sends out one man, that becomes his plan for making a living.
translations.idiomatic: Every envoy the court sends out treats the mission as his own livelihood.

sentences.zh: 虐取苛求，初無限量。

translations.literal: Cruel seizure and harsh demands know no limit from the start.
translations.idiomatic: Their cruel seizures and harsh demands know no limit.

sentences.zh: 有司承奉，惟恐不及。

translations.literal: Local officials carry out their wishes, fearing only that they will fall short.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials carry out their wishes, fearful only of falling short.

sentences.zh: 間有廉強自守、不事幹媚者，輒肆讒毀，動得罪譴，無以自明。

translations.literal: Occasionally there are those who are upright and strong in self-restraint and do not court favor; they are at once slandered without restraint, often punished and censured, with no way to clear themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Now and then an official who is upright and refuses to curry favor is slandered without restraint, punished, and left with no way to clear his name.

sentences.zh: 是以使者所至，有司公行貨賂，剝下媚上，有同交易。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever envoys arrive, officials openly practice bribery, stripping those below to please those above, like a transaction.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever envoys go, officials openly take bribes, squeezing those below to please those above, as if it were a trade.

sentences.zh: 夫小民所積幾何，而內外上下誅求如此。

translations.literal: How much can the common people accumulate, when inside and outside, above and below, extort like this?
translations.idiomatic: How much can common people possibly save when extortion from every level runs so deep?

sentences.zh: 今山東、河南、山西、陜西水旱相仍，民至剝樹皮掘草根以食。

translations.literal: Now in Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi flood and drought follow one another; the people have reached the point of stripping tree bark and digging grass roots to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Today in Shandong, Henan, Shanxi, and Shaanxi floods and droughts follow one another, and the people strip tree bark and dig up grass roots for food.

sentences.zh: 老幼流移，顛踣道路，賣妻鬻子以求茍活。

translations.literal: Old and young wander away; they fall prostrate on the roads, selling wives and children to seek a bare living.
translations.idiomatic: Old and young wander the roads, collapsing along the way, selling wives and children merely to stay alive.

sentences.zh: 而京師聚集僧道萬餘人，日耗廩米百餘石，此奪民食以養無用也。

translations.literal: Yet in the capital more than ten thousand monks and Daoists are gathered, consuming over a hundred shi of granary rice daily—this is taking the people's food to nourish the useless.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the capital more than ten thousand monks and Daoist priests are gathered, consuming over a hundred shi of granary rice each day—this is taking food from the people to feed the useless.

sentences.zh: 至報效軍士，朝廷厚與糧賜。

translations.literal: As for soldiers who have offered service in return, the court generously grants them grain and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: As for soldiers who have volunteered for service, the court grants them generous rations and rewards.

sentences.zh: 及使就役，乃驕傲橫恣，閑遊往來。

translations.literal: When they are put to duty, they are arrogant and overbearing, idly wandering to and fro.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when put to work they grow arrogant and overbearing, wandering about at leisure.

sentences.zh: 此皆奸詭之人，懼還原伍，假此規避，非真有報效之心也。

translations.literal: These are all treacherous and deceitful men, afraid of returning to their original units, who use this to evade duty—not men who truly have a heart to repay service.
translations.idiomatic: These are deceitful men who fear returning to their original units and use the arrangement to evade duty—they do not truly wish to serve.

sentences.zh: 朝廷歲令天下織錦、鑄錢，遣內官買馬外蕃，所出常數千萬，而所取曾不能一二。

translations.literal: Each year the court orders the realm to weave brocade and cast coin, and sends inner eunuchs to buy horses from foreign lands; what is spent often runs to tens of millions, while what is obtained can scarcely be one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Each year the court orders brocade woven and coin cast throughout the realm and sends palace eunuchs abroad to buy horses; expenditures run to tens of millions, yet what is obtained scarcely amounts to one or two in ten.

sentences.zh: 馬至雖多，類皆駑下。

translations.literal: Although many horses arrive, for the most part they are inferior and weak.
translations.idiomatic: Although many horses arrive, most are poor and weak.

sentences.zh: 責民牧養，騷擾殊甚。

translations.literal: The people are charged to pasture and rear them, and the harassment is extreme.
translations.idiomatic: The people are charged with pasturing them, and the harassment is severe.

sentences.zh: 及至死傷，輒令賠補。

translations.literal: When they die or are injured, the people are at once ordered to compensate.
translations.idiomatic: When horses die or are injured, the people are ordered to make compensation.

sentences.zh: 馬戶貧困，更鬻妻子。

translations.literal: Horse-keeping households are impoverished and again sell wives and children.
translations.idiomatic: Horse-keeping households are driven to poverty and again sell wives and children.

sentences.zh: 此尤害之大者。

translations.literal: This is especially among the greatest harms.
translations.idiomatic: This is among the greatest of harms.

sentences.zh: 漠北降人，賜居室，盛供帳，意欲招其同類也。

translations.literal: For surrendered people from north of the desert, dwellings are granted and lavish supplies provided, intending to attract their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Surrendered peoples from the northern steppe are given houses and lavish provisions, in the hope of attracting others of their kind.

sentences.zh: 不知來者皆懷窺覘，非真遠慕王化，甘去鄉士。

translations.literal: They do not know that those who come all harbor designs of reconnaissance, and do not truly admire the royal transformation from afar or willingly leave their native lands.
translations.idiomatic: They do not realize that those who come are scouting and probing—not men who truly admire civilization from afar or willingly leave their homelands.

sentences.zh: 宜求來朝之後，遣歸本國，不必留為後日子孫患。

translations.literal: After they have come to court, they should be sent back to their own countries and need not be kept to become a trouble for later generations.
translations.idiomatic: After they have paid court, they should be sent home and not kept on to become a trouble for later generations.

sentences.zh: 至宮觀禱祠之事，有國者所當深戒。

translations.literal: As for matters of palaces, shrines, and prayer sacrifices, those who hold a state ought to take deep warning.
translations.idiomatic: As for palace shrines and prayer sacrifices, rulers ought to take deep warning.

sentences.zh: 古人有言，淫祀無福。

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying: improper sacrifices bring no blessing.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that improper sacrifices bring no blessing.

sentences.zh: 況事無益以害有益，蠹財妄費者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when what is useless harms what is useful, corrupting wealth and spending it recklessly!
translations.idiomatic: How much more when useless practices harm what is useful, wasting wealth in vain!

sentences.zh: 凡此數事，皆下失民心，上違天意。

translations.literal: All these several matters are such that below the people lose their hearts, and above Heaven's intent is violated.
translations.idiomatic: All these matters alike cost you the people's hearts below and offend Heaven's intent above.

sentences.zh: 怨讟之興，實由於此。

translations.literal: The rise of resentment and slander truly stems from this.
translations.idiomatic: The rise of resentment and complaint truly stems from this.

sentences.zh: 夫奉天殿者，所以朝群臣，發號令，古所謂明堂也。

translations.literal: The Hall of Imperial Heaven is where the court assembles the ministers and issues commands—the ancient so-called Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Imperial Heaven is where the court assembles ministers and issues commands—the ancient Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 而災首及焉，非常之變也。

translations.literal: Yet disaster struck it first—an extraordinary change.
translations.idiomatic: Yet disaster struck it first—an extraordinary omen.

sentences.zh: 非省躬責己，大布恩澤，改革政化，疏滌天下窮困之人，不能回上天譴怒。

translations.literal: Unless Your Majesty examines yourself and blames yourself, broadly dispenses favor, reforms government and transformation, and clears away the destitute of the realm, Heaven's angry reproach cannot be turned back.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Your Majesty examines yourself, extends grace broadly, reforms government, and relieves the destitute throughout the realm, Heaven's angry reproach cannot be turned aside.

sentences.zh: 前有監生生員，以單丁告乞侍親，因而獲罪遣戍者，此實有虧治體。

translations.literal: Earlier there were Imperial Academy students who, as sole surviving sons, petitioned to serve their parents and for this were punished and sent to frontier garrison—this truly damages the body of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Imperial Academy students who, as sole surviving sons, petitioned to care for their parents were punished and sent to frontier garrison—this truly damages the dignity of governance.

sentences.zh: 近者大赦，法司執滯常條，當赦者尚復拘系。

translations.literal: Recently there was a great amnesty, yet the judicial offices clung to routine statutes, and those who should have been pardoned were still detained.
translations.idiomatic: After the recent great amnesty, the judicial offices clung to routine statutes, and men who should have been freed were still held.

sentences.zh: 並乞重加湔洗，蠲除租賦，一切勿征。

translations.literal: I also beg that cleansing be applied anew, rents and levies be remitted, and nothing at all be levied.
translations.idiomatic: I also beg that you cleanse these abuses anew, remit rents and levies, and levy nothing at all.

sentences.zh: 有司百官全其廩祿，拔簡賢才，申行薦舉，官吏貪贓蠹政者，核其罪而罷黜之。

translations.literal: Let all officials and the hundred offices keep their salaries intact; select the worthy; carry out recommendations; and for officials who are greedy, corrupt, and ruin government, examine their crimes and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Let all officials keep their salaries intact; select the worthy, carry out recommendations, and for greedy, corrupt officials who ruin government, examine their crimes and dismiss them.

sentences.zh: 則人心歡悅，和氣可臻，所以保安宗社，為國家千萬年無窮之基，莫有大於此者矣。

translations.literal: Then people's hearts will rejoice, harmonious qi can be attained, and thereby the ancestral altars can be secured—the foundation for the state's ten thousand years without end; nothing is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Then hearts will rejoice, harmony can be restored, and the ancestral altars secured—the foundation for the state's endurance through ten thousand years; nothing is greater than this.

sentences.zh: 且國家所恃以久長者，惟天命人心，而天命常視人心為去留。

translations.literal: Moreover, what the state relies on for long endurance is only Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts, and Heaven's mandate constantly regards the people's hearts for staying or departing.
translations.idiomatic: What the state relies on for long endurance is Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts, and Heaven's mandate follows the people's hearts in staying or departing.

sentences.zh: 今天意如此，不宜勞民。

translations.literal: Today Heaven's intent is thus; the people ought not to be burdened.
translations.idiomatic: Today Heaven's intent is clear; the people ought not to be burdened further.

sentences.zh: 當還都南京，奉謁陵廟，告以災變之故。

translations.literal: You should return the capital to Nanjing, pay respects at the tombs and temples, and report the reason for the calamitous change.
translations.idiomatic: You should return the capital to Nanjing, pay respects at the imperial tombs and temples, and report the reason for this calamity.

sentences.zh: 保養聖躬休息於無為。

translations.literal: Nurture the sacred person and rest in non-action.
translations.idiomatic: Nurture your sacred person and rest in non-action.

sentences.zh: 毋聽小人之言，復有所興作，以誤陛下於後也。

translations.literal: Do not heed petty men's words and undertake construction again, lest Your Majesty be misled hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Do not heed petty men's counsel and launch new works, lest Your Majesty be led astray hereafter.

sentences.zh: 書奏，不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; it received no attention.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but the throne took no notice.

sentences.zh: 時三殿初成，帝方以定都詔天下，忽罹火災，頗懼，下詔求直言。

translations.literal: At the time the three halls had just been completed; the Emperor had just proclaimed to the realm the fixing of the capital when fire suddenly struck, and he was rather afraid and issued an edict calling for forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: The three main halls had just been completed; the Emperor had just proclaimed the fixing of the capital when fire suddenly struck. Alarmed, he issued an edict calling for frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 及言者多斥時政，帝不懌，而大臣復希旨詆言者。

translations.literal: When many who spoke condemned current policy, the Emperor was displeased, and great ministers again curried favor by slandering those who spoke.
translations.idiomatic: When many memorials condemned current policy, the Emperor was displeased, and senior ministers again curried favor by attacking the critics.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，謂言事者謗訕，下詔嚴禁之，犯者不赦。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon grew angry, saying that those who spoke on affairs were slandering, and issued an edict strictly forbidding it; offenders would not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor thereupon grew angry, declaring that critics were slandering the throne, and issued an edict strictly forbidding such speech; offenders would not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 侍讀李時勉、侍講羅汝敬俱下獄；

translations.literal: Reader-in-Waiting Li Shimian and Reader-in-Waiting Luo Rujing were both imprisoned;
translations.idiomatic: Reader-in-Waiting Li Shimian and Reader-in-Waiting Luo Rujing were both imprisoned;

sentences.zh: 御史鄭維桓、何忠、羅通、徐容，給事中柯暹俱左官交阯。

translations.literal: Censors Zheng Weiheng, He Zhong, Luo Tong, and Xu Rong, and Supervising Secretary Ke Xian were all demoted and sent to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zheng Weiheng, He Zhong, Luo Tong, and Xu Rong, and Supervising Secretary Ke Xian were all demoted and sent to Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 惟緝與主事高公望、庶吉士楊復得無罪。

translations.literal: Only Ji, Chief Clerk Gao Gongwang, and Bachelor-in-Waiting Yang Fu were found not guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Only Zou Ji, Chief Clerk Gao Gongwang, and Hanlin Bachelor Yang Fu escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，緝進右庶子兼侍講。

translations.literal: That winter, Ji was promoted to Right Vice-Director of the Household and concurrently Reader-in-Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zou Ji was promoted to Right Vice-Director of the Household and concurrently Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 明年九月卒於官。

translations.literal: The following year in the ninth month he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: The following September he died in office.

sentences.zh: 緝博極群書，居官勤慎，清操如寒士。

translations.literal: Ji was broadly learned in all books, diligent and careful in office, with pure integrity like a poor scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Ji had mastered every branch of learning, served with diligence and care, and maintained the pure integrity of a poor scholar.

sentences.zh: 子循，宣德中為翰林待詔，請贈父母。

translations.literal: His son Xun, during the Xuande reign served as Hanlin Awaiting Imperial Decree and petitioned to posthumously ennoble his parents.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xun served as a Hanlin awaiting imperial decree during the Xuande reign and petitioned for posthumous honors for his parents.

sentences.zh: 帝諭吏部曰：「曩皇祖征沙漠，朕守北京，緝在左右，陳說皆正道，良臣也，其予之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed the Ministry of Personnel, saying: "Formerly when my imperial ancestor campaigned in the desert and I held Beijing, Ji was at my side; everything he presented was the correct path—a worthy minister. Grant his request."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the Ministry of Personnel: "When my imperial ancestor campaigned in the desert and I held Beijing, Zou Ji was at my side. Everything he counseled was sound—he is a worthy minister. Grant his request."

sentences.zh: 鄭維桓，慈溪人。

translations.literal: Zheng Weiheng was a native of Cixi.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Weiheng came from Cixi.

sentences.zh: 永樂十三年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the palace examination in Yongle 13.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in Yongle 13 (1415).

sentences.zh: 出知交阯南清州，卒。

translations.literal: Was sent out as prefect of Nanqing Prefecture in Jiaozhi and died there.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Nanqing Prefecture in Jiaozhi, where he died.

sentences.zh: 柯暹，池州建德人。

translations.literal: Ke Xian was a native of Jiande in Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ke Xian came from Jiande in Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 由鄉舉出知交阯州。

translations.literal: Through the provincial examination, was sent out as prefect of Jiaozhi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Through the provincial examination he was sent out as prefect of Jiaozhi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 累官浙江、雲南按察使。

translations.literal: Rose through offices to Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to serve as Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 弋謙，代州人。

translations.literal: Yi Qian was a native of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian came from Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂九年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the palace examination in Yongle 9.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in Yongle 9 (1411).

sentences.zh: 除監察御史。

translations.literal: Was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 出按江西，言事忤旨，貶峽山知縣。

translations.literal: Was sent out to inspect Jiangxi; his memorials on affairs offended the imperial intent and he was demoted to magistrate of Xiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to inspect Jiangxi, he memorialized on affairs in a way that offended the throne and was demoted to magistrate of Xiashan.

sentences.zh: 復坐事免歸。

translations.literal: Again because of an affair was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was again dismissed over an affair and returned home.

sentences.zh: 仁宗在東宮，素知謙骨鯁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ren was in the Eastern Palace, he had long known Qian's stiff bones.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Ren was heir apparent, he had long known Yi Qian's uncompromising integrity.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，召為大理少卿。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Qian was summoned as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, Yi Qian was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 直陳時政，言官吏貪殘，政事多非洪武之舊，及有司誅求無藝。

translations.literal: He spoke forthrightly on current policy, saying that officials were greedy and cruel, that government affairs largely departed from Hongwu practice, and that local offices extracted demands without limit.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke forthrightly on current affairs, declaring that officials were greedy and cruel, that government had largely departed from Hongwu practice, and that local offices extorted without restraint.

sentences.zh: 帝多采納。

translations.literal: The Emperor mostly adopted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor largely adopted his recommendations.

sentences.zh: 既復言五事，詞太激，帝乃不懌。

translations.literal: Then he again spoke on five matters; his language was too harsh and the Emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: When he again raised five matters, his language was too harsh and the Emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 尚書呂震、吳中，侍郎吳廷用，大理卿虞謙等因劾謙誣罔，都御史劉觀令眾御史合糾謙。

translations.literal: Ministers Lu Zhen and Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Wu Tingyong, Court of Judicial Review Minister Yu Qian, and others thereupon impeached Qian for falsehood; Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan ordered all censors jointly to impeach Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Lu Zhen and Wu Zhong, Vice Minister Wu Tingyong, Court of Judicial Review Minister Yu Qian, and others thereupon impeached Yi Qian for deceit, and Censor-in-Chief Liu Guan ordered the censors jointly to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 帝召楊士奇等言之，士奇對曰：「謙不諳大體，然心感超擢恩，欲圖報耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Yang Shiqi and others to speak of it. Shiqi replied: "Qian does not understand the larger pattern, yet his heart is moved by the grace of his extraordinary promotion and he wishes to repay it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned Yang Shiqi and others to discuss the matter. Shiqi replied: "Yi Qian does not grasp the larger pattern, yet his heart is moved by the grace of his sudden promotion and he wishes to repay it.

sentences.zh: 主聖則臣直，惟陛下優容之。

translations.literal: When the ruler is sage then ministers are straight; I beg Your Majesty to be indulgent toward him.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler is sage, ministers speak straight; I beg Your Majesty to be indulgent toward him.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃不罪謙。

translations.literal: " The Emperor thereupon did not punish Qian.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor thereupon did not punish Yi Qian.

sentences.zh: 然每見謙，詞色甚厲。

translations.literal: Yet whenever he saw Qian, his words and expression were very harsh.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever he saw Yi Qian, his words and manner were very harsh.

sentences.zh: 士奇從容言：「陛下詔求直言，謙言不當，觸怒。

translations.literal: Shiqi said calmly: "Your Majesty issued an edict seeking forthright speech; Qian's words were inappropriate and provoked anger.
translations.idiomatic: Shiqi said calmly: "Your Majesty issued an edict seeking forthright speech. Yi Qian spoke inappropriately and provoked Your Majesty's anger.

sentences.zh: 外廷悚惕，以言為戒。

translations.literal: The outer court is fearful and wary, taking speech as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: The outer court is fearful and wary, taking speech as a warning.

sentences.zh: 今四方朝覲之臣皆集闕下，見謙如此，將謂陛下不能容直言。

translations.literal: Now officials coming to court from the four quarters are all gathered below the palace gate; seeing Qian treated thus, they will think Your Majesty cannot tolerate forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Officials from all quarters are now gathered below the palace gate. Seeing Yi Qian treated thus, they will conclude that Your Majesty cannot tolerate forthright speech.

sentences.zh: 」帝惕然曰：「此固朕不能容，亦呂震輩迎合以益朕過，自今當置之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor said soberly: "This is indeed my lack of tolerance, and also Lu Zhen and his ilk currying favor and adding to my fault; from now I should set this aside.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said soberly: "This is indeed my failure to be tolerant, and Lu Zhen and his ilk have curried favor and added to my fault. From now on I should set this aside.

sentences.zh: 」遂免謙朝參，令專視司事。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Qian was exempted from court attendance and ordered to concentrate solely on his duties.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon Yi Qian was exempted from court attendance and ordered to concentrate solely on his official duties.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝以言事者益少，復召士奇曰：「朕怒謙矯激過實耳，朝臣遂月餘無言。

translations.literal: Before long, because memorialists grew fewer, the Emperor again summoned Shiqi and said: "My anger at Qian was only over his exaggeration and excess; yet court officials went more than a month without speaking.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, seeing that fewer officials were speaking up, the Emperor again summoned Shiqi and said: "My anger at Yi Qian was only over his exaggeration and excess, yet court officials went more than a month without speaking.

sentences.zh: 爾語諸臣，白朕心。

translations.literal: You speak to the officials and explain my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Speak to the officials and explain my intent.

sentences.zh: 」士奇曰：「臣空言不足信，乞親降璽書。

translations.literal: " Shiqi said: "My empty words are insufficient for credence; I beg that Your Majesty personally issue an imperial letter.
translations.idiomatic: " Shiqi said: "My words alone will not be believed. I beg that Your Majesty personally issue an imperial letter.

sentences.zh: 」遂令就榻前書敕引過曰：「朕自即位以來，臣民上章以數百計，未嘗不欣然聽納。

translations.literal: " He was then ordered to write at the bedside an edict acknowledging fault, saying: "Since I ascended the throne, officials and people have submitted memorials numbering in the hundreds, and I have never failed to hear and accept them gladly.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then ordered to draft at the bedside an edict acknowledging fault, which read: "Since I ascended the throne, officials and commoners have submitted memorials numbering in the hundreds, and I have never failed to hear and accept them gladly.

sentences.zh: 茍有不當，不加譴訶，群臣所共知也。

translations.literal: If any were inappropriate, I did not add rebuke—this all the officials know together.
translations.idiomatic: When any were inappropriate, I did not add rebuke—all the officials know this.

sentences.zh: 間者，大理少卿弋謙所言，多非實事，群臣迎合朕意，交章奏其賣直，請置諸法。

translations.literal: Recently, Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yi Qian spoke much that was not factual; officials curried my favor and jointly memorialized that he was selling integrity, asking that he be punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Vice Minister of the Court of Judicial Review Yi Qian spoke much that was not factual. Officials curried my favor and jointly memorialized that he was selling integrity and asked that he be punished by law.

sentences.zh: 朕皆拒而不聽，但免謙朝參。

translations.literal: I refused all this and did not listen, but only exempted Qian from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: I refused all of this, but only exempted Yi Qian from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 而自是以來，言者益少。

translations.literal: Yet since then, those who speak have grown fewer still.
translations.idiomatic: Yet since then, those who speak up have grown fewer still.

sentences.zh: 今自去冬無雪，春亦少雨，陰陽愆和，必有其咎，豈無可言？

translations.literal: Now since last winter there has been no snow, and spring too has had little rain; yin and yang are out of harmony—there must be some fault; can there be nothing to say?
translations.idiomatic: Now since last winter there has been no snow and spring too has had little rain. Yin and yang are out of harmony—there must be some fault. Can there truly be nothing worth saying?

sentences.zh: 而為臣者，懷自全之計，退而默默，何以為忠？

translations.literal: Yet as ministers, harboring plans for self-preservation and withdrawing in silence—how is that loyalty?
translations.idiomatic: Yet as ministers, if you harbor plans for self-preservation and withdraw in silence, how is that loyalty?

sentences.zh: 朕于謙一時不能含容，未嘗不自愧咎。

translations.literal: Toward Qian I could not for a time contain myself, and I have never failed to feel ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Toward Yi Qian I could not for a time contain myself, and I have never ceased to feel ashamed.

sentences.zh: 爾群臣勿以前事為戒，於國家利弊、政令未當者，直言勿諱。

translations.literal: You officials must not take the previous affair as a warning; where the state's benefit or harm and policy orders are not right, speak forthrightly without reserve.
translations.idiomatic: You officials must not take the previous affair as a warning. Where the state's interests are at stake or policy is wrong, speak forthrightly without reserve.

sentences.zh: 謙朝參如故。

translations.literal: Qian's court attendance is as before.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian's court attendance is restored as before.

sentences.zh: 」時中官采木四川，貪橫。

translations.literal: " At the time eunuchs were procuring timber in Sichuan, greedy and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time eunuchs were procuring timber in Sichuan, acting with greed and overbearing violence.

sentences.zh: 帝以謙清直，命往治之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because Qian was pure and upright, ordered him to go govern it.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yi Qian was pure and upright, the Emperor ordered him to go and put a stop to it.

sentences.zh: 擢謙副都御史，賜鈔以行，遂罷采木之役。

translations.literal: Qian was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, given paper money for the journey, and the timber-procurement corvée was thereupon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Qian was promoted to Vice Censor-in-Chief, given paper money for the journey, and the timber-procurement corvée was thereupon abolished.

sentences.zh: 宣德初，交阯右布政戚遜以貪淫黜，命謙往代。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuande, Right Provincial Administrator of Jiaozhi Qi Xun was dismissed for greed and licentiousness; Qian was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xuande reign, Right Provincial Administrator of Jiaozhi Qi Xun was dismissed for greed and licentiousness, and Yi Qian was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 王通棄交阯，謙亦論死。

translations.literal: Wang Tong abandoned Jiaozhi, and Qian was also sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tong abandoned Jiaozhi, Yi Qian was also sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 正統初，釋為民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong he was released to be a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengtong reign he was released to live as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，謙布衣走闕下，薦通及寧懋、阮遷等十三人，皆奇才可用。

translations.literal: At the Tumu crisis, Qian in commoner's garb hurried to the palace gate and recommended Tong and Ning Mao, Ruan Qian, and thirteen others in all—all extraordinary talents who could be employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the Tumu crisis, Yi Qian in commoner's garb hurried to the palace gate and recommended Wang Tong, Ning Mao, Ruan Qian, and thirteen others in all—extraordinary talents fit for service.

sentences.zh: 眾議以通副石亨，謙請專任通，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The assembly debated making Tong deputy to Shi Heng; Qian asked that Tong be given sole responsibility, and the matter thereupon lapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly debated making Wang Tong deputy to Shi Heng, but Yi Qian asked that Tong be given sole responsibility, and the matter lapsed.

sentences.zh: 廷臣以謙負重名，奏留之，亦不報。

translations.literal: Court officials, because Qian bore a great reputation, memorialized to keep him—this too received no response.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials, because Yi Qian bore a great reputation, memorialized to retain him, but this too received no response.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年復至京，疏薦通等，不納。

translations.literal: In Jingtai 2 he again came to the capital and submitted a memorial recommending Tong and others; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 2 (1451) he again came to the capital and submitted a memorial recommending Wang Tong and others, but it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，未幾卒。

translations.literal: He resigned and returned home and soon died.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned and returned home, and soon died.

sentences.zh: 仁宗性寬大，容直言，謙以故得無罪，反責呂震等。

translations.literal: Emperor Ren was by nature magnanimous and tolerated forthright speech; Qian for this reason escaped punishment, and the Emperor instead blamed Lu Zhen and others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ren was by nature magnanimous and tolerated forthright speech; Yi Qian for this reason escaped punishment, and the Emperor instead blamed Lu Zhen and others.

sentences.zh: 而黃驥言西域事，帝亦誚震而行其言。

translations.literal: When Huang Ji spoke on Western Regions affairs, the Emperor also rebuked Zhen and carried out his words.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Ji spoke on Western Regions affairs, the Emperor also rebuked Lu Zhen and carried out Ji's recommendations.

sentences.zh: 驥，全州人。

translations.literal: Ji was a native of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ji came from Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，中鄉舉。

translations.literal: During Hongwu he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 為沙縣教諭。

translations.literal: He served as instructor of Shaxian.
translations.idiomatic: He served as instructor of Shaxian.

sentences.zh: 永樂時擢禮科給事中，常三使西域。

translations.literal: In the Yongle reign he was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Ritual Section and was thrice sent as envoy to the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yongle reign he was promoted to Supervising Secretary of the Ritual Section and was thrice sent as envoy to the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初，上疏言：「西域貢使多商人假托，無賴小人投為從者，乘傳役人，運貢物至京師，賞賚優厚。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ren's reign, he submitted a memorial saying: "Western Regions tribute envoys are mostly merchants falsely posing as such; worthless petty men attach themselves as followers, commandeer relay horses and press men into service, transport tribute goods to the capital, and receive generous rewards.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ren's reign, he submitted a memorial saying: "Western Regions tribute envoys are mostly merchants falsely posing as such. Worthless petty men attach themselves as followers, commandeer relay horses and press men into service, transport tribute goods to the capital, and receive generous rewards.

sentences.zh: 番人慕利，貢無虛月，致民失業妨農。

translations.literal: Barbarians covet profit; tribute comes nearly every month, causing the people to lose their livelihoods and hampering agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier peoples covet profit, and tribute missions come nearly every month, causing the people to lose their livelihoods and hampering agriculture.

sentences.zh: 比其使還，多賫貨物，車運至百餘輛。

translations.literal: When their envoys return, they mostly carry goods away, with carts numbering more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When their envoys return, they mostly carry goods away in more than a hundred carts.

sentences.zh: 丁男不足，役及婦女。

translations.literal: When adult males are insufficient, corvée extends even to women.
translations.idiomatic: When adult males are insufficient, corvée labor extends even to women.

sentences.zh: 所至辱驛官，鞭夫隸，無敢與較者。

translations.literal: Wherever they go they humiliate relay officials and whip laborers and clerks; none dare contend with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever they go they humiliate relay officials and whip laborers and clerks, and none dare stand up to them.

sentences.zh: 乞敕陜西行都司，惟哈密諸國王遣使入貢者，許令來京，止正副使得乘驛馬，陜人庶少蘇。

translations.literal: I beg that the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission be commanded: only when kings of states such as Hami send envoys to offer tribute should they be permitted to come to the capital; only the chief and deputy envoys should be allowed relay horses—and the people of Shaanxi can thus breathe somewhat easier.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Shaanxi Regional Military Commission be ordered: only when kings of states such as Hami send envoys to offer tribute should they be permitted to come to the capital, and only the chief and deputy envoys should be allowed relay horses—so that the people of Shaanxi may breathe somewhat easier.

sentences.zh: 至西域所產，惟馬切邊需，應就給甘肅軍士。

translations.literal: As for Western Regions products, only horses are urgently needed on the frontier; these should be distributed directly to the Gansu garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Of Western Regions products, only horses are urgently needed on the frontier; these should be distributed directly to the Gansu garrison troops.

sentences.zh: 其碙砂、梧桐、鹼之類，皆無益國用，請一切勿受，則來者自稀，浮費益省。

translations.literal: Sal ammoniac, parasol trees, alkali, and the like all benefit state use not at all; I ask that none of these be accepted—then comers will naturally grow scarce and wasteful expenditure be further reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Sal ammoniac, parasol trees, alkali, and the like all benefit state use not at all. I ask that none of these be accepted—then visitors will naturally grow scarce and wasteful expenditure be further reduced.

sentences.zh: 」帝以示尚書呂震，且讓之曰：「驥嘗奉使，悉西事。

translations.literal: " The Emperor showed it to Minister Lu Zhen and moreover rebuked him, saying: "Ji has served on missions and knows Western affairs thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor showed the memorial to Minister Lu Zhen and rebuked him, saying: "Huang Ji has served on missions and knows Western affairs thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 卿西人，顧不悉邪？

translations.literal: You are a native of the west—do you not know them?
translations.idiomatic: You are a native of the west—do you not know these matters?

sentences.zh: 驥言是，其即議行。

translations.literal: Ji's words are correct; immediately deliberate and implement them.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ji's words are correct. Deliberate at once and implement them.

sentences.zh: 」後遷右通政，與李琦、羅汝敬撫諭交阯，不辱命。

translations.literal: " Later he was transferred to Right Administrator and, together with Li Qi and Luo Rujing, went to pacify and instruct Jiaozhi without disgracing the commission.
translations.idiomatic: " Later he was transferred to Right Administrator and, together with Li Qi and Luo Rujing, went to pacify and instruct Jiaozhi without disgracing the commission.

sentences.zh: 使還，尋卒。

translations.literal: After completing the mission and returning, he soon died.
translations.idiomatic: After completing the mission and returning, he soon died.

sentences.zh: 黃澤，閩縣人。

translations.literal: Huang Ze was a native of Min County.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ze came from Min County.

sentences.zh: 永樂十年進士。

translations.literal: Passed the palace examination in Yongle 10.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the palace examination in Yongle 10 (1412).

sentences.zh: 擢河南左參政。

translations.literal: Was promoted to Left Provincial Administrator of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Left Provincial Administrator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 南陽多流民，拊循使復業。

translations.literal: In Nanyang there were many displaced persons; he comforted and guided them to resume their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Nanyang had many displaced persons; he comforted and guided them back to their occupations.

sentences.zh: 嘗率丁役至北京，周恤備至。

translations.literal: Once he led corvée laborers to Beijing and showed them every consideration.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he led corvée laborers to Beijing, he showed them every consideration.

sentences.zh: 久之，調湖廣。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was transferred to Huguang.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was transferred to Huguang.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，入覲，言時政，多見采。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ren ascended the throne, he entered audience, spoke on current policy, and much was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ren ascended the throne, he came to audience, spoke on current affairs, and much of what he said was adopted.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，下詔求言。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he issued an edict seeking counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong came to the throne, he issued an edict seeking counsel.

sentences.zh: 澤上疏言正心、恤民、敬天、納諫、練兵、重農、止貢獻、明賞罰、遠嬖幸、汰冗官十事。

translations.literal: Ze submitted a memorial on ten matters: rectifying the heart, caring for the people, reverencing Heaven, accepting remonstrance, drilling troops, valuing agriculture, halting tribute offerings, clarifying rewards and punishments, keeping distance from favorites, and eliminating redundant officials.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Ze submitted a memorial on ten matters: rectifying the heart, caring for the people, reverencing Heaven, accepting remonstrance, drilling troops, valuing agriculture, halting tribute offerings, clarifying rewards and punishments, keeping distance from favorites, and eliminating redundant officials.

sentences.zh: 其言遠嬖幸曰：「刑余之人，其情幽陰，其慮險譎。

translations.literal: On keeping distance from favorites he said: "Men punished by mutilation—their dispositions are dark and hidden, their designs treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: On keeping distance from favorites he said: "Men punished by mutilation have dispositions that are dark and hidden and designs that are treacherous.

sentences.zh: 大奸似忠，大詐似信，大巧似愚。

translations.literal: Great treachery resembles loyalty, great deceit resembles faithfulness, great cunning resembles foolishness.
translations.idiomatic: Great treachery resembles loyalty, great deceit resembles faithfulness, and great cunning resembles foolishness.

sentences.zh: 一與之親，如飲醇酒，不知其醉；

translations.literal: Once intimate with them, it is like drinking fine wine without knowing one is drunk;
translations.idiomatic: Once you grow close to them, it is like drinking fine wine without knowing you are drunk;

sentences.zh: 如噬甘臘，不知其毒。

translations.literal: it is like eating sweet cured meat without knowing its poison.
translations.idiomatic: it is like eating sweet cured meat without knowing its poison.

sentences.zh: 寵之甚易，遠之甚難。

translations.literal: To favor them is very easy; to keep them distant is very hard.
translations.idiomatic: To favor them is very easy; to keep them at a distance is very hard.

sentences.zh: 是以古者宦寺不使典兵幹政，所以防患於未萌也。

translations.literal: Therefore in antiquity palace eunuchs were not allowed to command troops or meddle in government—this was to guard against trouble before it sprouted.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in antiquity palace eunuchs were not allowed to command troops or meddle in government—this was to guard against trouble before it sprouted.

sentences.zh: 涓涓弗塞，將為江河。

translations.literal: A trickle unblocked becomes a river.
translations.idiomatic: A trickle left unblocked becomes a river.

sentences.zh: 此輩宜一切疏遠，勿使用事。

translations.literal: This sort should all be kept at a distance and not employed in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: This sort should all be kept at a distance and not employed in affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 漢、唐已事，彰彰可監。

translations.literal: The precedents of Han and Tang are shining and may serve as mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: The precedents of Han and Tang stand plain and may serve as mirrors.

sentences.zh: 」當成祖時，宦官稍稍用事，宣宗浸以親幸。

translations.literal: " During the Yongle Emperor's time eunuchs gradually began to wield power; Emperor Xuanzong increasingly favored them.
translations.idiomatic: " During the Yongle Emperor's reign eunuchs gradually began to wield power, and Emperor Xuanzong increasingly favored them.

sentences.zh: 澤於十事中此為尤切。

translations.literal: Among the ten matters this was especially pointed from Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Among the ten matters, this was Huang Ze's most pointed counsel.

sentences.zh: 帝雖嘉嘆，不能用也。

translations.literal: The Emperor though he praised and sighed could not employ it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and sighed over it, but could not put it into practice.

sentences.zh: 其後設內書堂，而中人多通書曉文義。

translations.literal: Afterward the Inner Calligraphy Hall was established, and eunuchs mostly mastered writing and understood literary meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Inner Calligraphy Hall was established, and eunuchs mostly mastered writing and understood literary meaning.

sentences.zh: 宦寺之盛，自宣宗始。

translations.literal: The great flourishing of palace eunuchs began with Emperor Xuanzong.
translations.idiomatic: The great flourishing of palace eunuchs began with Emperor Xuanzong.

sentences.zh: 宣德三年擢浙江布政使。

translations.literal: In Xuande 3 he was promoted to Provincial Administrator of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 3 (1428) he was promoted to Provincial Administrator of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 復上言平陽、麗水等七縣銀冶宜罷，並請盡罷諸坑冶，語甚切。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that the silver smelteries of the seven counties including Pingyang and Lishui ought to be abolished, and also asked that all mining operations be wholly abolished; his language was very pointed.
translations.idiomatic: He again memorialized that the silver smelteries of the seven counties including Pingyang and Lishui ought to be abolished, and also asked that all mining operations be wholly abolished; his language was very pointed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘆息曰：「民困若此，朕何由知？

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed and said: "The people are in such distress—how am I to know?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sighed and said: "The people are in such distress—how am I to know?

sentences.zh: 遣官驗視，酌議以聞。

translations.literal: Send officials to inspect and verify, discuss measures as appropriate, and report.
translations.idiomatic: Send officials to inspect and verify, discuss appropriate measures, and report back.

sentences.zh: 」澤在官有政績，然多暴怒，鹽運使丁鎡不避道，撻之，為所奏。

translations.literal: " Ze while in office had administrative achievements, yet was often violently angry; the Salt Transport Commissioner Ding Zan did not yield the road and was flogged—he was impeached for it.
translations.idiomatic: " While serving in office, Ze had administrative achievements, yet he was often violently angry; the Salt Transport Commissioner Ding Zan did not yield the road and was flogged, and Ze was impeached for it.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史馬謹亦劾澤九載秩滿，自出行縣，斂白金三千兩償官物，且越境過家。

translations.literal: The touring investigating censor Ma Jin also impeached Ze: after nine years his term was complete, he went out personally to inspect counties, collected three thousand taels of white silver to repay official goods, and moreover crossed district boundaries to visit his home.
translations.idiomatic: The touring investigating censor Ma Jin also impeached Ze: after nine years his term was complete, he went out personally to inspect the counties, collected three thousand taels of white silver to repay official goods, and moreover crossed district boundaries to visit his home.

sentences.zh: 遂逮下獄。

translations.literal: He was thereupon arrested and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon arrested and imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 正統六年黜為民。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 6 he was dismissed and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 6 (1441) he was dismissed and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 初，澤奏金華、臺州戶口較洪武時耗減，而歲造弓箭如舊，乞減免。

translations.literal: Previously, Ze had memorialized that the registered population of Jinhua and Taizhou had declined compared to the Hongwu era, while the annual manufacture of bows and arrows remained as before, and he begged for reduction and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Ze had memorialized that the registered population of Jinhua and Taizhou had declined compared to the Hongwu era, while the annual manufacture of bows and arrows remained unchanged, and he begged for reduction and exemption.

sentences.zh: 下部議得允，而澤已罷官逾月矣。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated and approval was granted, but Ze had already been removed from office for more than a month.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry deliberated and approval was granted, but Ze had already been removed from office for more than a month.

sentences.zh: 孔友諒，長洲人。

translations.literal: Kong Youliang came from Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Youliang came from Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 永樂十六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi in Yongle 16.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Yongle 16 (1418).

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，出知雙流縣。

translations.literal: Transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, then sent out as magistrate of Shuangliu County.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Hanlin Bachelor, then sent out as magistrate of Shuangliu County.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初，上言六事：

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, he submitted a memorial on six matters:
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Xuanzong's reign, he submitted a memorial on six matters:

sentences.zh: 一曰，守令親民之官，古者不拘資格，必得其人；

translations.literal: First, prefects and magistrates are officials close to the people; in antiquity they did not rigidly bound by qualifications—they had to obtain the right person;
translations.idiomatic: First, prefects and magistrates are officials close to the people; in antiquity they did not rigidly bound by qualifications—they had to obtain the right person;

sentences.zh: 不限歲月，使盡其力。

translations.literal: Without limiting the months, they were made to exhaust their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Without limiting their term in months, they were made to exert their full strength.

sentences.zh: 今居職者多不知撫字之方，而廉幹得民心者，又遷調不常，差遣不一。

translations.literal: Today those holding office mostly do not know the methods of comforting and nourishing the people, while those who are incorrupt and capable and win the hearts of the people are again transferred irregularly and dispatched on various assignments.
translations.idiomatic: Today those holding office mostly do not know how to comfort and nourish the people, while those who are incorrupt, capable, and win the people's hearts are transferred irregularly and dispatched on various assignments.

sentences.zh: 或因小事連累，朝夕營治，往來道路，日不暇給。

translations.literal: Sometimes because of minor matters they are implicated, morning and evening managing affairs, traveling back and forth on the roads—the day scarcely suffices.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes they are implicated over minor matters, managing affairs morning and evening and traveling back and forth on the roads, with scarcely a moment to spare.

sentences.zh: 乞敕吏部，擇才望素優及久歷京官者任之。

translations.literal: I beg that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to select those of outstanding talent and reputation and those long experienced in capital office to appoint them.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Ministry of Personnel be ordered to select those of outstanding talent and reputation and those long experienced in capital office to appoint them.

sentences.zh: 諭戒上司，毋擅差遣，假以歲月，責成治效。

translations.literal: Admonish and warn their superiors not to dispatch them on their own authority, grant them time in months and years, and hold them accountable for governing achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Admonish and warn their superiors not to dispatch them on their own authority, grant them sufficient time, and hold them accountable for governing achievements.

sentences.zh: 至遠缺佐貳，多經裁減，獨員居職。

translations.literal: As for distant deputy posts, many have been cut by reductions, with a single incumbent holding the position alone.
translations.idiomatic: As for distant deputy posts, many have been cut by reductions, leaving a single incumbent to hold the position alone.

sentences.zh: 或遇事赴京，多委雜職署事，因循茍且，政令無常，民不知畏。

translations.literal: Sometimes when something arises and one goes to the capital, many entrust miscellaneous subordinates to act in their stead—procrastinating perfunctorily, government orders without constancy, the people unaware of what to fear.
translations.idiomatic: Sometimes when urgent business requires a trip to the capital, many entrust miscellaneous subordinates to act in their stead—procrastinating perfunctorily, government orders without constancy, and the people unaware of what to fear.

sentences.zh: 今後路遠之缺，常留一正員任事，不得擅離，庶法有常守。

translations.literal: From now on for distant vacancies, regularly leave one regular incumbent in charge of affairs, who may not leave without authorization—then the law will have a constant guardian.
translations.idiomatic: From now on, for distant vacancies, regularly leave one regular incumbent in charge of affairs, who may not leave without authorization—then the law will have a constant guardian.

sentences.zh: 二曰，科舉所以求賢，必名實相副，非徒誇多而已。

translations.literal: Second, the civil service examinations are for seeking the worthy—they must match name and reality, not merely boast of quantity.
translations.idiomatic: Second, the civil service examinations are meant to seek the worthy—they must match name and reality, not merely boast of quantity.

sentences.zh: 今秋闈取士動一二百人。

translations.literal: Today at the autumn provincial examinations scholars taken number one or two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Today at the autumn provincial examinations, one or two hundred scholars are selected.

sentences.zh: 弊既多端，僥幸過半。

translations.literal: Abuses are many-sided; more than half pass by luck.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses are manifold; more than half pass by sheer luck.

sentences.zh: 會試下第，十常八九，其登第者，實行或乖。

translations.literal: Of those who fail the metropolitan examination, nine or eight out of ten; of those who pass, actual conduct is often at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Of those who fail the metropolitan examination, eight or nine out of ten; of those who pass, actual conduct is often at odds.

sentences.zh: 請於開科之歲，詳核諸生行履。

translations.literal: I ask that in years when examinations open, thoroughly verify the conduct and records of students.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that in years when examinations are held, the conduct and records of students be thoroughly verified.

sentences.zh: 孝弟忠信、學業優贍者，乃許入試。

translations.literal: Only those filial, respectful to elders, loyal, trustworthy, and superior in learning and substance—only these may be permitted to enter the examination.
translations.idiomatic: Only those filial, respectful to elders, loyal, trustworthy, and superior in learning and substance may be permitted to enter the examination.

sentences.zh: 庶浮薄不致濫收，而國家得真才之用。

translations.literal: Then the frivolous and shallow will not be indiscriminately enrolled, and the state will obtain the employment of true talent.
translations.idiomatic: Then the frivolous and shallow will not be indiscriminately enrolled, and the state will obtain the employment of true talent.

sentences.zh: 三曰，祿以養廉，祿入過薄，則生事不給。

translations.literal: Third, salary is to nurture integrity—if salary income is too thin, then daily affairs cannot be supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Third, salary is to nurture integrity—if salary income is too meager, then daily needs cannot be met.

sentences.zh: 國朝制祿之典，視前代為薄。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's system of salary allotments is thin compared to previous ages.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's system of salary allotments is thin compared to previous ages.

sentences.zh: 今京官及方面官稍增俸祿，其餘大小官自折鈔外，月不過米二石，不足食數人。

translations.literal: Today capital officials and regional officials have had salaries somewhat increased; the remaining officials large and small, apart from converted paper money, have no more than two shi of rice per month—not enough to feed several people.
translations.idiomatic: Today capital officials and regional officials have had their salaries somewhat increased; the remaining officials large and small, apart from converted paper money, receive no more than two shi of rice per month—not enough to feed several people.

sentences.zh: 仰事俯育，與道路往來，費安所取資？

translations.literal: Supporting parents above and nurturing children below, and travel on the roads—where does the expense come from?
translations.idiomatic: Supporting parents above and nurturing children below, and traveling on the roads—where does the money come from?

sentences.zh: 貪者放利行私，廉者終窶莫訴。

translations.literal: The greedy profit privately through usury; the incorrupt end destitute with none to whom they can appeal.
translations.idiomatic: The greedy profit privately through usury; the incorrupt end destitute with no one to whom they can appeal.

sentences.zh: 請敕戶部勘實天下糧儲，以歲支之余，量增官俸。

translations.literal: I ask that the Ministry of Revenue be ordered to verify truthfully the grain stores throughout the realm, and from the surplus of annual disbursements, measure an increase to official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Ministry of Revenue be ordered to verify truthfully the grain stores throughout the realm, and from the surplus of annual disbursements, measure an increase to official salaries.

sentences.zh: 仍令內外風憲官，采訪廉潔之吏，重加旌賞。

translations.literal: Also order internal and external circuit censors to investigate and collect information on incorrupt officials and greatly add commendations and rewards.
translations.idiomatic: Also order internal and external circuit censors to investigate and commend incorrupt officials with substantial rewards.

sentences.zh: 則廉者知勸，貪者知戒。

translations.literal: Then the incorrupt will know encouragement, the greedy will know warning.
translations.idiomatic: Then the incorrupt will know encouragement, and the greedy will know warning.

sentences.zh: 四曰，古者賦役量土宜，驗丁口，不責所無，不盡所有。

translations.literal: Fourth, in antiquity taxes and corvée were measured to local suitability, verified by household registers—not demanding what was not had, not exhausting all that was possessed.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, in antiquity taxes and corvée were measured to local suitability and verified by household registers—not demanding what was not had, not exhausting all that was possessed.

sentences.zh: 今自常賦外，復有和買、采辦諸事。

translations.literal: Today beyond the regular taxes, there are again cooperative purchasing, procurement, and various other matters.
translations.idiomatic: Today beyond the regular taxes, there are again cooperative purchasing, procurement, and various other matters.

sentences.zh: 自朝廷視之，不過令有司支官錢平買。

translations.literal: From the court's perspective, it is merely ordering local officials to disburse official funds to purchase at fair prices.
translations.idiomatic: From the court's perspective, it is merely ordering local officials to disburse official funds to purchase at fair prices.

sentences.zh: 而無賴之輩，關通吏胥，壟斷貨物，巧立辨驗、折耗之名，科取數倍，奸弊百端。

translations.literal: But rascals collude with clerks and runners, monopolize goods, ingeniously establish names such as verification and loss allowance, levying several times the amount—abuses of every kind.
translations.idiomatic: But rascals collude with clerks and runners, monopolize goods, ingeniously establish names such as verification and loss allowance, levying several times the amount—abuses of every kind.

sentences.zh: 乞盡停采買，減諸不急務，則國賦有常，民無科擾。

translations.literal: I beg that procurement be wholly halted and various non-urgent affairs reduced—then state levies will have constancy and the people will be free from irregular exactions.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that procurement be wholly halted and various non-urgent affairs reduced—then state levies will have constancy and the people will be free from irregular exactions.

sentences.zh: 其二事言汰冗員，任風憲，言者多及之，不具載。

translations.literal: His other two items spoke of eliminating redundant posts and appointing circuit censors—many memorialists also touched on these; they are not fully recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: His other two items spoke of eliminating redundant posts and appointing circuit censors—many memorialists also touched on these; they are not fully recorded here.

sentences.zh: 宣德八年，命吏部擇外官有文學者六十八人試之，得友諒及進士胡端禎等七人，悉令辦事六科。

translations.literal: In Xuande 8 the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to select sixty-eight external officials of literary accomplishment to test them; Youliang was obtained, together with jinshi Hu Duanzhen and six others—all were ordered to handle affairs in the Six Offices of Scrutiny.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 8 (1433) the Ministry of Personnel was ordered to select sixty-eight external officials of literary accomplishment to test them; Youliang was obtained, together with jinshi Hu Duanzhen and six others—all were ordered to handle affairs in the Six Offices of Scrutiny.

sentences.zh: 居二年，皆授給事中，惟友諒未授官而卒。

translations.literal: After two years, all were appointed supervising secretaries; only Youliang died before receiving appointment.
translations.idiomatic: After two years, all were appointed supervising secretaries; only Youliang died before receiving appointment.

sentences.zh: 範濟，元進士。

translations.literal: Fan Ji was a jinshi of the Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ji was a jinshi of the Yuan.

sentences.zh: 洪武中，以文學舉為廣信知府，坐累謫戍興州。

translations.literal: In the Hongwu era he was recommended for literary accomplishment and appointed Prefect of Guangxin; implicated in a case he was banished to garrison duty at Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu era he was recommended for literary accomplishment and appointed Prefect of Guangxin; implicated in a case he was banished to garrison duty at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，濟年八十餘矣，詣闕言八事：

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Ji was already over eighty; he came to the palace gates and submitted a memorial on eight matters:
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Ji was already over eighty; he came to the palace gates and submitted a memorial on eight matters:

sentences.zh: 其一曰楮幣之法，昉於漢、唐。

translations.literal: The first spoke of the method of paper currency, which began in Han and Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The first spoke of the method of paper currency, which began in Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 元造元統交鈔，後又造中統鈔。

translations.literal: The Yuan minted Yuantong Jiaochao, and later also minted Zhongtong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan minted Yuantong Jiaochao, and later also minted Zhongtong Chao.

sentences.zh: 久而物重鈔輕，公私俱敝，乃造至元鈔與中統鈔兼行。

translations.literal: After long time goods were heavy and notes light—public and private alike were exhausted; they then minted Zhiyuan Chao to circulate jointly with Zhongtong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time goods were heavy and notes light—public and private alike were exhausted; they then minted Zhiyuan Chao to circulate jointly with Zhongtong Chao.

sentences.zh: 子母相權，新陳通用。

translations.literal: Parent and child notes counterbalanced each other; new and old were universally used.
translations.idiomatic: Parent and child notes counterbalanced each other; new and old were universally used.

sentences.zh: 又令民間以昏鈔赴平準庫，中統鈔五貫得換至元鈔一貫。

translations.literal: They also ordered the people to bring worn notes to the Stabilization Office—five strings of Zhongtong Chao could be exchanged for one string of Zhiyuan Chao.
translations.idiomatic: They also ordered the people to bring worn notes to the Stabilization Office—five strings of Zhongtong Chao could be exchanged for one string of Zhiyuan Chao.

sentences.zh: 又其法日造萬錠，共計官吏俸稍、內府供用若干，天下正稅雜課若干，斂發有方，周流不滯，以故久而通行。

translations.literal: Furthermore their law minted ten thousand ingots daily; totaling official salaries of officials, inner-palace supplies, regular taxes and miscellaneous levies throughout the realm—collection and issuance had method, circulation without stagnation; for this reason it circulated for long.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore their law minted ten thousand ingots daily; totaling official salaries, inner-palace supplies, regular taxes and miscellaneous levies throughout the realm—collection and issuance had method, circulation without stagnation; for this reason it circulated for long.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝造大明寶鈔。

translations.literal: The Taizu Emperor minted the Da Ming Treasure Note.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hongwu minted the Da Ming Treasure Note.

sentences.zh: 以鈔一貫當白金一兩，民歡趨之。

translations.literal: One note string equaled one tael of white silver; the people gladly rushed to use it.
translations.idiomatic: One note string equaled one tael of white silver; the people gladly rushed to use it.

sentences.zh: 迄今五十餘年，其法稍弊，亦由物重鈔輕所致。

translations.literal: To this day more than fifty years—the method has slightly deteriorated, also because goods are heavy and notes light.
translations.idiomatic: To this day more than fifty years have passed—the method has slightly deteriorated, also because goods are heavy and notes light.

sentences.zh: 願陛下因時變通，重造寶鈔，一準洪武初制，使新舊兼行。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty, adapting to circumstances and changing with the times, would remint Treasure Notes according to the initial Hongwu system, making new and old circulate jointly.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty, adapting to circumstances and changing with the times, would remint Treasure Notes according to the initial Hongwu system, making new and old circulate jointly.

sentences.zh: 取元時所造之數而增損之，審國家度支之數而權衡之。

translations.literal: Take the quantity minted in Yuan times and increase or decrease it; examine the state's expenditure figures and weigh them.
translations.idiomatic: Take the quantity minted in Yuan times and increase or decrease it; examine the state's expenditure figures and weigh them.

sentences.zh: 俾鈔少而物多，鈔重而物輕。

translations.literal: Thus notes would be few and goods many, notes heavy and goods light.
translations.idiomatic: Thus notes would be few and goods many, notes heavy and goods light.

sentences.zh: 嚴偽造之條，開倒換之法，推陳出新，無耗無阻，則鈔法流通，永永無弊。

translations.literal: Strictly enforce provisions against counterfeiting, open methods of exchange, pushing out the old and bringing in the new—without loss, without obstruction—then the note system would circulate, forever without defect.
translations.idiomatic: Strictly enforce provisions against counterfeiting, open methods of exchange, pushing out the old and bringing in the new—without loss, without obstruction—then the note system would circulate, forever without defect.

sentences.zh: 其二曰備邊之道，守險為要。

translations.literal: The second spoke of the way to prepare the frontier—holding perilous passes is essential.
translations.idiomatic: The second spoke of the way to prepare the frontier—holding perilous passes is essential.

sentences.zh: 若朔州、大同、開平、宣府、大寧，乃京師之藩垣，邊僥之門戶。

translations.literal: Such as Shuozhou, Datong, Kaiping, Xuanfu, Daning—these are the bulwark of the capital, the gateways of the border marches.
translations.idiomatic: Such as Shuozhou, Datong, Kaiping, Xuanfu, and Daning—these are the bulwark of the capital, the gateways of the border marches.

sentences.zh: 士可耕，城可守。

translations.literal: The land can be cultivated; the cities can be defended.
translations.idiomatic: The land can be cultivated; the cities can be defended.

sentences.zh: 宜盛兵防禦，廣開屯田，修治城堡，謹烽火，明斥堠。

translations.literal: It is fit to mass troops for defense, broadly open garrison farming, repair and maintain fortresses, carefully maintain beacon fires, make clear the outpost stations.
translations.idiomatic: It is fit to mass troops for defense, broadly open garrison farming, repair and maintain fortresses, carefully maintain beacon fires, and make clear the outpost stations.

sentences.zh: 毋貪小利，毋輕遠求，堅壁清野，使無所得。

translations.literal: Do not covet small profit, do not lightly seek far—fortify walls and clear the countryside, so they obtain nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Do not covet small profit, do not lightly seek far—fortify walls and clear the countryside, so they obtain nothing.

sentences.zh: 俟其憊而擊之，得利則止，毋窮追深入。

translations.literal: Wait until they are weary and then strike; if profit is gained then stop—do not pursue deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until they are weary and then strike; if profit is gained then stop—do not pursue deeply.

sentences.zh: 此守邊大要也。

translations.literal: This is the great gist of guarding the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: This is the great gist of guarding the frontier.

sentences.zh: 其三曰兵不在多，在於堪戰。

translations.literal: The third says troops are not in quantity but in being fit for battle.
translations.idiomatic: The third says troops are not in quantity but in being fit for battle.

sentences.zh: 比者多發為事官吏人民充軍塞上，非白面書生，則老弱病廢。

translations.literal: Recently many officials and people involved in cases have been sent to fill military service on the frontier—if not pale-faced bookish scholars, then old, weak, sick, and disabled.
translations.idiomatic: Recently many officials and people involved in cases have been sent to fill military service on the frontier—if not pale-faced bookish scholars, then old, weak, sick, and disabled.

sentences.zh: 遇有征行，有力者得免，貧弱者備數。

translations.literal: When there is a campaign, the strong can avoid it; the poor and weak fill the numbers.
translations.idiomatic: When there is a campaign, the strong can avoid it; the poor and weak fill the numbers.

sentences.zh: 器械不完，糗糧不具。

translations.literal: Weapons incomplete; dried rations not provided.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons incomplete; dried rations not provided.

sentences.zh: 望風股栗，安能效死？

translations.literal: Seeing the wind they tremble in their legs—how can they be expected to fight to the death?
translations.idiomatic: At the sight of the enemy they tremble in their legs—how can they be expected to fight to the death?

sentences.zh: 今宜選其壯勇，勤加訓練，余但令乘城擊柝，趨走牙門，庶幾各得其用。

translations.literal: Now it is fit to select the stalwart and brave, diligently train them; the rest need only be ordered to mount the walls and strike the night-watch clapper, run to the gate headquarters—then each will mostly obtain his use.
translations.idiomatic: Now it is fit to select the stalwart and brave and train them diligently; the rest need only be ordered to mount the walls and strike the night-watch clapper and run to the gate headquarters—then each will mostly obtain his use.

sentences.zh: 其四曰民病莫甚於勾軍。

translations.literal: The fourth says no suffering of the people is greater than military household conscription verification.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth says no suffering of the people is greater than military household conscription verification.

sentences.zh: 衛所差官至六七員，百戶差軍旗亦二三人，皆有力交結及畏避征調之徒，重賄得遣。

translations.literal: Guard posts send as many as six or seven officials; company commanders send two or three military bannermen—all are men with powerful connections and those who fear and evade levies, obtaining dispatch through heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Guard posts send as many as six or seven officials; company commanders send two or three military bannermen—all are men with powerful connections and those who fear and evade levies, obtaining dispatch through heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 既至州縣，擅作威福，迫脅裏甲，恣為奸私。

translations.literal: Once they arrive at prefecture and county, they arbitrarily wield authority, coerce the tithing heads, and indulge in private wrongdoing.
translations.idiomatic: Once they arrive at prefecture and county, they arbitrarily wield authority, coerce the tithing heads, and indulge in private wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 無丁之家，誅求不已；

translations.literal: Households without quota sons are extorted without end;
translations.idiomatic: Households without quota sons are extorted without end;

sentences.zh: 有丁之戶，詐稱死亡。

translations.literal: households with quota sons falsely claim death.
translations.idiomatic: households with quota sons falsely claim death.

sentences.zh: 托故留滯，久而不還。

translations.literal: Using excuses they delay and linger, long without returning.
translations.idiomatic: Using excuses they delay and linger, long without returning.

sentences.zh: 及還，則以所得財物，遍賄官吏，朦朧具覆。

translations.literal: When they return, they use the goods obtained to bribe officials everywhere, and muddle through with perfunctory reports.
translations.idiomatic: When they return, they use the goods obtained to bribe officials everywhere, and muddle through with perfunctory reports.

sentences.zh: 究其所取之丁，十不得一，欲軍無缺伍難矣。

translations.literal: Investigating the quota sons actually taken—ten do not yield one; to wish the army without depleted ranks is difficult indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating the quota sons actually taken—ten do not yield one; to wish the army without depleted ranks is difficult indeed.

sentences.zh: 自今軍士有故，令各衛報都督府及兵部，府、部諜布政、按察司。

translations.literal: From now when soldiers have affairs, order each guard to report to the Chief Military Commission and Ministry of War; the commission and ministry notify the provincial administration and surveillance commissions.
translations.idiomatic: From now when soldiers have affairs, order each guard to report to the Chief Military Commission and Ministry of War; the commission and ministry notify the provincial administration and surveillance commissions.

sentences.zh: 令府州縣準籍貫姓名，勾取送衛，則差人騷擾之弊自絕。

translations.literal: Order prefectures, departments, and counties according to registered domicile and name to conscript and deliver to the guard—then the abuse of dispatching personnel causing harassment will of itself cease.
